channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: RBSA On Tour at Winterbourne House Exhibition 2026 · Royal Birmingham Society of Artists
item.description: Free members' exhibition taking RBSA work out of the gallery and into Winterbourne House, the Edwardian house and botanic garden in Birmingham, for a four-and-a-half month run from October 10, 2026 to February 28, 2027. Open only to RBSA Members, Associates and Honorary Members; work may have been shown at the RBSA Gallery before, and pieces from the recent Members and Associates Small Works Exhibition are especially welcome. All styles and media are eligible including photography and digital work, where digital technology is an essential part of the artistic process — but not giclee or other reproductions of handmade originals, and not AI-generated images. Every print, digital ones included, must be editioned with the edition size clearly stated. Artists may submit up to four works, with at least two each expected to hang and the Winterbourne House curatorial team selecting if the show is oversubscribed. All work must be under 65cm in every dimension including the frame, made in the past three years, priced at no more than £695 and for sale for the full run. There are no entry fees and no display fees. — Deadline: September 8, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition at Winterbourne House.

item.title: The PASEO 2027 Biennial · The Paseo Project
item.description: Twelfth edition of the outdoor festival that turns the streets of the Taos Historic District into a night-time gallery of installation, projection and performance, across the evenings of Friday and Saturday, September 17–18, 2027. Around twenty works are selected. The 2027 theme is Convergence — movement toward connection, the dynamic space between individuality and collectivity where difference, contradiction and multiplicity coexist; rivers converge without abandoning their sources, cultures converge while carrying memory forward. Work must be immersive, site-responsive and/or participatory, built for outdoor viewing after dark, and already fully realised: The PASEO does not fund new commissions or undeveloped concepts. Selected artists receive a stipend of $500–$3,000 for standard projects, rising to $5,000–$15,000 for larger works depending on scope and impact, with travel, lodging, shipping, installation assistance and equipment covered and an artist fee set to W.A.G.E. standards. Artists must be present from sunset to 11pm on both nights, and are invited to propose adult and youth workshops, lectures and forums as part of the application. Open to emerging, mid-career and professional artists over 21 from anywhere in the world. — Deadline: November 1, 2026. Fee: $25 (free for Taos County residents). Prize: $500–$15,000 stipend.

item.title: Hawaiʻi Nei 2026 — 18th Annual Exhibition · Hawaii Island Art Alliance
item.description: Annual juried exhibition at the Wailoa Center in Hilo devoted to the native species of Hawai'i Island — organisms that arrived naturally by wind, waves or wings, whether endemic to Hawai'i or indigenous to Hawai'i and elsewhere. Artwork whose main subject is a non-native species, a Polynesian introduction, or a native species found only on other Hawaiian islands is not accepted, and work made from materials taken from an endangered native species is excluded. Any medium is welcome, with separate adult categories for two-dimensional work, three-dimensional work and photography, plus a youth section that is free to enter. Reproductions and AI-generated or AI-assisted work are not accepted; pieces must have been made in the past four years and not previously shown at the Wailoa Center, and because the gallery is a State Parks facility work with nudity or offensive religious, political or violent content may be juried out. Open to residents of Hawai'i Island only. Emily Catey Weiss, program director at the Volcano Art Center and previously a working photographer on Oahu's North Shore, juries the adult divisions; Erzsi Kuba Palko, illustrator of two books on native Hawaiian species, juries the youth divisions. The jurors ask for an artist statement describing your pilina — your relationship to the species, to the island and to the piece itself — and say it may weigh in the selection. The show runs November 6 – December 10, 2026, opening with a reception on November 6, with awards presented alongside a small makana for every participating artist. Sold work is split 60% to the artist, 40% to the organisers. — Deadline: October 9, 2026. Fee: $20 per entry (free under 18). Prize: Exhibition at Wailoa Center.

item.title: 2026 Call for Exhibiting Artists · Baton Rouge Gallery
item.description: Baton Rouge Gallery — center for contemporary art, founded in 1966 and one of America's oldest artist cooperatives — opens its annual application to join a roster of more than 75 Exhibiting Artists working across a wide range of media. Members show in the gallery's 2,800 square foot space, keep 60% of all sales of their work, are represented on the gallery website, get a discount at Mo's Art Supply, and have a genuine voice in how the organisation runs: exhibiting artists vote on which special exhibitions to host and which artists to invite to join. In return, members exhibit at least once every three years in month-long shows, help with receptions, talks and installation, and pay $100 in annual dues, with opportunities to offset that cost; membership is reviewed every five years. Open to artists 18 and over who are at least two years removed from formal art education — no student work or work made under supervision — and who can show Louisiana residency or explain their relationship to Baton Rouge or the state; once accepted, artists may keep their membership if they move away. Applications are juried in two rounds on craftsmanship, originality, quality of presentation and professional experience. — Deadline: September 10, 2026. Fee: $5. Prize: Cooperative gallery exhibition.

item.title: HOPE · The Studio Door
item.description: Juried exhibition running September 25 – November 6, 2026 at The Studio Door, the gay-owned and operated gallery in San Diego. The brief is a single question — what gives you hope? — with no prescribed message or point of view: the gallery is looking for authentic work capable of making a lasting connection with the people who see it, work collectors will want to live with. Painting, drawing, photography, printmaking, assemblage, collage, mixed media, fibre art, artist books and sculpture are all accepted; performance art is not, and video, film, installation or anything requiring an external power source needs gallery approval before submitting. An entry is one to three artworks, all of which must be available for sale and arrive gallery-ready, with black or natural wood frames preferred. Juror Patric Stillman, the gallery's founder, juried the 2025 Oceanside Museum of Art Biennial, writes a monthly arts column for The WORD San Diego and received the 2024 Larry T. Baza Arts & Culture Award from San Diego Pride; he gives three Juror's Awards of $100 each. Gallery space is limited, so not every accepted submission can be hung. Open to Southern California visual artists; artists are notified by September 4 and are responsible for hand delivery on September 19 and pickup in November. Sales are split 50/50 with the gallery. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: $35 (1 work), $40 (2), $45 (3). Prize: Three $100 Juror's Awards + exhibition.

item.title: 20/20 Vision: A 20th Anniversary Exhibition · Artists of Palm Beach County
item.description: Twentieth-anniversary show from Artists of Palm Beach County, presented at Studio 1608 in West Palm Beach, an art destination that has become a gathering place for artists, collectors and enthusiasts across the county. Abstract, representational, contemporary, traditional and experimental work are all welcome. Every piece must be in a 20 x 20 inch format: work on paper should be adhered to a 20 x 20 canvas, photographs may be printed on canvas or metal, and three-dimensional work must fit within a 20 x 20 inch footprint, though height may vary. Artists may submit up to three works, all of which must be for sale at the price given at submission — that price cannot be changed later — with members receiving 75% of the gross. Explicitly sexual or political work is not accepted, and neither is anything created with artificial intelligence. Membership is not required to enter but lowers the fee. Irina Rothenberg, an art collector and advisor at Findlay Galleries, judges, awarding $150 for first place, $100 for second and $50 for third. Artists are notified on or before September 9; work is delivered September 14, the opening reception is September 19 and the closing reception October 17, 2026. — Deadline: September 4, 2026. Fee: $30 members / $40 non-members. Prize: $150 / $100 / $50.

item.title: Lubbock Arts Festival Juried Gallery 2027 · Lubbock Arts Alliance
item.description: Juried gallery of the 49th Lubbock Arts Festival, held April 10–11, 2027 in the Lubbock Memorial Civic Center and open to artists working in any fine art medium, photography included. Entries must be original in design and execution, completed within the last two years, and not made in a workshop or under supervision; each artist may enter up to ten works, of which no more than three will be shown. Juror Rob Weingart has taught foundations, 2D and 3D art at West Texas A&M University for the past decade and previously worked in the gallery and museum world in New York, Chicago and London, with a BFA from the University of North Texas and an MFA from the School of the Art Institute of Chicago. Up to $1,000 in cash prizes is awarded at the juror's discretion. Accepted work must be hand delivered — shipped artwork is not accepted — ready to hang securely on wire with no sawtooth hangers, no larger than 44 x 72 inches framed and under 35 pounds. All work must be for sale at the submitted price with sales tax included; the Lubbock Arts Alliance retains a 33 1/3% commission, and artists must obtain a Texas sales tax number in order to enter. — Deadline: March 1, 2027. Fee: $30 per entry. Prize: Up to $1,000 in cash prizes.

item.title: GLEAN 2026/27
item.description: Juried program giving five Portland-area artists five months of access to the Metro Central transfer station — the dump — to glean discarded materials and make work from them. Selected artists receive a $3,000 stipend, studio visits, marketing support and group critiques with GLEAN artists and partners, culminating in a group exhibition. Gleaning runs November 2026 to March 2027, with on-site safety training and orientation on November 2, 2026 and the exhibition in April/May 2027. Each artist must produce at least eight pieces for sale at the exhibition, with 95% of each piece made from gleaned materials, and keeps 80% commission on sales; Recology and Metro each retain one unpurchased piece, and studio space is not provided. For a third year, one of the five places goes to an artist selected for exceptional craft, supported by the Rainmaker Craft Initiative. One residency position is reserved for a student currently enrolled in an art program at a local college or university, considered separately from other applications, and artists working in a variety of media are encouraged to apply. GLEAN is a partnership between Recology Oregon Recovery, Metro — the regional government that manages the Portland area's garbage and recycling system — and the environmental arts nonprofit ReClaim It, and has run since 2010. — Deadline: September 13, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $3,000 stipend + Exhibition.

item.title: Hotel Willa Artist-in-Residence 2027 · The Paseo Project
item.description: Four-week self-directed residency at Hotel Willa in Taos, New Mexico, activated by The Paseo Project, for the months of February, March, April, July, August, October, November and December 2027. The hotel — a 1940s motel reimagined as an art-forward destination in the historic district, five minutes' walk from Taos Plaza — hosts one artist at a time. Residents get a private one-bedroom suite with kitchenette, a private on-site studio outfitted with work surfaces, easel, sink, desk lamp, rolling cart and cutting mat, a bicycle for the duration, and restaurant discounts and vouchers. There is no stipend: artists cover travel, materials and meals, and a car is recommended. Artists are invited to give an artist talk and open studio on the third Thursday of their stay. Open to artists, makers, writers and creatives in all disciplines who live or work in the Four Corners region or within a 300-mile radius of Taos; Taos County residents are not eligible, and the program cannot accommodate couples or families. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: 4-week residency.

item.title: Delfina Foundation — Central & West Africa Curators Residency 2027
item.description: Six- or twelve-week residency in London during Delfina Foundation's winter 2027 'open' season (5 January – 28 March 2027), for curators based in Central and West Africa, supported by Delfina's Network of Patrons for Africa. Support covers a return economy flight, UK airport transfers, reimbursement of visa fees, a £40 per day living allowance, a £70 per week materials and research allowance, a London travel pass, and a single bedroom with desk in Delfina's house, which hosts up to eight residents around a shared kitchen, library and dining room. The programme includes guided visits to museums, galleries, non-profits and artist-run spaces, trips to institutions outside London, organised presentations and studio visits, portfolio reviews and mentoring. Applicants must hold nationality of and be based in one of 26 listed countries, have at least five years of professional curatorial practice — independent, institutional or academic — and be proficient in English, as the interview is conducted in English. Curators with an artistic background are welcome, but the residency is not open to applicants whose primary practice is as an artist. — Deadline: August 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Funded residency + £40/day living allowance.

item.title: Patchwork · Kinhouse Gallery
item.description: Juried exhibition at Kinhouse Gallery in Fort Wayne, Indiana, inspired by quilts and the art of piecing things together. Work may respond to the quilt as literal artwork, as technique (piecing, patchwork, appliqué, stitching in any medium), or as visual language — grids, blocks, repeated motifs and pattern-based composition, even outside fiber art. All mediums are accepted, and work engaging pattern, texture, scrap and reuse, and the handmade is especially encouraged. Selected artists receive a $20 shipping stipend and inclusion in the published Patchwork Catalog alongside an extended selection of submitted work. Exhibition October 2–30, 2026, opening during the Arts This Way Broadway Arts Festival; 20% commission on sales. — Deadline: August 23, 2026. Fee: $12. Prize: Exhibition + Catalog publication.

item.title: diptych/triptych/multiples/collage · A Smith Gallery
item.description: A Smith Gallery's juried online exhibition for work built from more than one frame — diptychs, triptychs, multiples and collages. The gallery's premise is that diptychs tell stories, triptychs tell larger stories, and multiples and collages tell larger ones still. Juror Manuela Thames is a Saint Paul–based photographic artist, born and raised in Germany, whose largely self-taught, contemplative practice explores loss and grief, generational trauma, belonging and connection; her work has been recognised by the Monovisions Awards and a Julia Margaret Cameron Award, and she teaches for Santa Fe Workshops, SE Center for Photography, Maine Media and LACP. Jurying is blind. Up to 47 images are selected for the online exhibition and catalogue, with 27 chosen for 'The 27', a hardbound fine-art book. The Juror's Award and Directors' Award each carry an online solo exhibition, 'The 27' and a blog feature; a Visitors' Award of $100 goes to the most Instagram likes. Photographers submitting 13 or more images receive a complimentary director review. Open to professional and amateur photographers worldwide in all photographic mediums; work previously exhibited at A Smith Gallery is ineligible. Online exhibition 1 November – 31 December 2026, reception 28 November. — Deadline: October 5, 2026. Fee: $40/5 images + $5 each. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Blank Wall Gallery — Moments of Color
item.description: Open call on colour — the bold contrast of urban life, the soft pastels of a sunset, the vibrant hues of nature — asking how photographers capture the essence of colour in their work and turn ordinary moments into something extraordinary. Free to submit; selected photographers pay a participation fee only if exhibited (€35 if the photograph is printed, €15 if it is shown on the gallery's 43-inch 4K digital screen). Over 100 printed photographs are shown in each exhibition, with printing on 260 gsm paper, framing, hanging, invitations and the opening night all covered by the gallery, and no commission taken on sales. Selected work is shown at Blank Wall Gallery in Athens, 23 October – 4 November 2026. — Deadline: September 18, 2026. Fee: Free (€15–€35 if accepted). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Blank Wall Gallery — Still Life
item.description: International open call devoted to still life — classic or contemporary, minimal or conceptual — where composition, light and detail turn everyday objects, natural elements and arranged scenes into work that carries beauty, emotion and meaning. Free to submit; selected photographers pay a participation fee only if exhibited (€35 if the photograph is printed, €15 if it is shown on the gallery's 43-inch 4K digital screen). Over 100 printed photographs are shown in each exhibition, with printing on 260 gsm paper, framing, hanging, invitations and the opening night all covered by the gallery, and no commission taken on sales. Selected work is shown at Blank Wall Gallery in Athens, 20 November – 2 December 2026. — Deadline: October 22, 2026. Fee: Free (€15–€35 if accepted). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Picture This — 2026 Photography Show · San Marcos Art League
item.description: The San Marcos Art League gives over its Art Center gallery for the month of August to a show dedicated entirely to the photographic medium, from traditional film work to contemporary digital compositions. Entry is open to all and each entrant may submit one artwork; accepted work must be hand-delivered ready to hang at the San Marcos Art Center on Sunday 2 August between 1pm and 4pm, since shipped work is not accepted. Work must be original, signed and completed in the previous 24 months, and must not have been shown at the Art Center Gallery before. Two-dimensional pieces are capped at 36 inches wide by 68 inches high including framing, and everything must be for sale, with the Art League retaining a 20% commission. The exhibition runs 5–28 August 2026 with a public opening reception on Friday 7 August from 6 to 8pm. — Deadline: July 31, 2026. Fee: $20 ($10 members). Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: San Marcos Arts Festival Juried Art Exhibition 2026
item.description: The juried exhibition anchoring the San Marcos Arts Festival, presented by the San Marcos Art League on behalf of the City of San Marcos and open to artists in any fine art media, photography included. The juror is Margo Handwerker, Director of the Glassell School of Art at the Museum of Fine Arts, Houston, previously Dean of its Core Residency Program and Chief Curator and Director of the Texas State Galleries in San Marcos; she holds a PhD from Princeton's School of Architecture and is a practising artist and member of the M12 Studio collective. Up to $500 in cash prizes is awarded at the juror's discretion. Artists may submit up to five entries but no more than two works can appear in the show, and work must have been completed in the last two years. Accepted work must be hand-delivered on 1 November — nothing shipped — framed no larger than 36 by 48 inches and under 35 pounds. The exhibition runs 4–20 November 2026 at the San Marcos Art Center, with an opening reception on 13 November and the festival itself on 14 November. All work must be for sale; the Art League retains a 20% commission. — Deadline: August 17, 2026. Fee: $30 per entry. Prize: Up to $500 in cash prizes + Group exhibition.

item.title: Erbleichen · NEU!
item.description: NEU! is an artist-run space on Untere Vogelsangstrasse in Winterthur with a curated programme of a new show every two months. For a group exhibition in November 2026 it is looking for work from a world that flows thick and slow and is losing its colour — spaces where time seems to stand still and the future and its promises go unfulfilled, time loops, system errors, ghosts, doppelgängers of decay. The great bleaching. Proposals are welcome across all mediums and may be unfinished, unproduced, in process or complete, and are sent by email. There is no entry fee. NEU! notes that it is not able to cover shipping or similar costs. — Deadline: July 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: Aurora 2026 Members Juried Exhibition
item.description: Aurora PhotoCenter, the artist-run photography centre in Indianapolis, opens its main gallery to its own membership for a juried show that treats photography as broadly as possible — all work that incorporates photography, in any subject, style or working method, will be considered. Barbara Tannenbaum, Chair of Prints, Drawings and Photographs and Curator of Photography at the Cleveland Museum of Art, is the juror; she organised over 80 exhibitions across 26 years at the Akron Art Museum before joining Cleveland in 2011, where her shows include Ilse Bing: Queen of the Leica and DIY: Photographers & Books, the first museum exhibition of print-on-demand photobooks. Any member current as of 31 August may send up to five images, noting print size, framing, capture method (35mm, 120, 4x5, DSLR, phone or other) and date. Submitting costs nothing beyond membership, and artists living outside Indiana can join through Aurora's $35 Distance membership. Aurora makes all decisions about printing, matting, framing, layout and pricing, and prints and prepares accepted work for the wall from existing frame stock free of charge. Work is priced at no more than $300; artists keep 70% of any sale or can donate the proceeds to Aurora. The show runs 4 December 2026 to 15 January 2027 with an opening reception on 4 December. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: Free for members. Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: periscope:project:space Open Call 2027
item.description: periscope is an artist-run project space in Salzburg that has been programming exhibitions, performances and site-specific work since 2014, and it is assembling its 2027 season through an open call to Austrian and international visual artists. Three lines of interest are named: solo presentations of an artist's own practice shown as premieres, projects that respond to the space or the site itself, and performance as part of an artistic practice. Depending on the project, periscope covers production costs, pays expenses for transport, travel and accommodation, and pays an exhibition fee — an unusually concrete offer for a small independent space. Submissions are digital only and consist of documentation of the work, a proposal or sketches of up to 400 words, and a CV. There is no entry fee and no theme beyond the three interest areas; past programmes have included lens-based and photographic projects alongside installation and sound work. — Deadline: July 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Solo exhibition + Artist fee.

item.title: Local Testimony 2026 · Edut Mekomit
item.description: The annual Israeli press and documentary photography exhibition, founded in 2003 and shown each year at MUZA — Eretz Israel Museum in Tel Aviv, in parallel with World Press Photo. The 2026 contest opens on 13 August and closes at midnight on 31 August. Single images may be entered in six fields — News (open only to holders of a GPO or Israeli Journalists Union press card), Religion and Faith, Society and Community, Urbanism and Culture, Sport, and Nature and Environment — up to ten photographs per field. Alongside singles there are three other formats: short series (up to four series of four to six photographs each, no press card required), Long Exposure (a documentary story built over more than a year, ten to fifteen photographs, at least three from the past year), and video works up to seven minutes made in 2025–2026. The curator of the 2026 edition is Ilia Yefimovich, a documentary maker and AFP staff photographer. Entry is free. Grants totalling 30,000 NIS are split equally between Photo of the Year (the Roi Idan Prize, given by the Israeli Journalists Union), Series of the Year, and Video Work of the Year — the last a production grant from Shomrim, the Center for Media and Democracy, dedicated to making a new video work with the Shomrim newsroom for the 2027 exhibition. Every photographer in the exhibition receives the catalogue and a certificate of participation. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: 30,000 NIS cash + Group exhibition.

item.title: MonoVisions Black & White Photography Awards 2027
item.description: The 2027 cycle of MonoVisions Magazine's international monochrome competition is open. Work is entered either as a single photograph or as a series of up to eight images sharing one idea, across twelve categories: Abstract, Architecture, Conceptual, Fine Art, Landscapes, Nature and Wildlife, Nude, People, Photojournalism, Portrait, Street Photography and Travel. Both traditional and digital black-and-white photography are accepted, and the competition is open to professionals and amateurs alike. The prize fund is $5,000, split between Black and White Series of the Year ($3,000) and Black and White Photo of the Year ($2,000); category winners and honourable mentions receive badges and certificates rather than additional cash. Fees are tiered by deadline — $20 for a single photo and $25 for a series until the early deadline of 17 January 2027, then $25 and $30 until the final deadline of 16 May 2027. Winners are announced on 25 July 2027 and judged by a panel of thirteen international photographers and artists. — Deadline: May 16, 2027. Fee: $20–$30. Prize: $5,000.

item.title: 13th Annual LA Billboard Exhibition: No Walls · The Billboard Creative
item.description: For thirteen years The Billboard Creative has turned billboards across Los Angeles into a citywide open-air gallery, buying the same advertising space that usually sells products and giving it to artists instead. Selected artists each receive their own billboard in Los Angeles for four weeks; TBC covers production, installation and the billboard space itself, and photographs each installed board for its exhibition archive. Boards are placed on high-traffic routes near galleries, museums and cultural centres as well as on ordinary commuter roads, so the work is seen by people who would not otherwise walk into a gallery — past exhibitions have been covered by NPR, Hyperallergic, the Los Angeles Times and KCRW. Photography is explicitly welcome alongside painting, sculpture, collage, mixed media and digital work: if the piece can be supplied as a digital file it can go on a billboard. Video and audio works are not accepted for this edition. Entries cost $28 for the first image and $10 for each additional image up to twenty. — Deadline: November 22, 2026. Fee: $28 first image + $10 each addl. Prize: Billboard exhibition in LA.

item.title: Sea to Shining Sea · Albrecht-Kemper Museum of Art
item.description: A national juried exhibition of the American landscape in all media at the Albrecht-Kemper Museum of Art in Saint Joseph, Missouri, on view from 21 November 2026 to 21 February 2027. Artists may submit up to three works, each juried and scored individually, with a maximum size of 60 by 60 inches and 50 pounds. The juror is Lisa Grossman, a painter and printmaker based in Lawrence, Kansas since 1996 whose work follows the prairies and river valleys of eastern Kansas; she has had more than thirty solo shows across the Midwest and on both coasts and is represented by Haw Contemporary in Kansas City and SNW Gallery in Manhattan, Kansas. Awards are chosen after the exhibition is hung: $500 Best of Show, $250 second, $150 third and a $100 People's Choice. Open to artists 18 and over; AI-generated work is not considered. Work may be shipped (arriving by 10 November with a prepaid return label) or hand-delivered on 16 November. Work need not be for sale, but the museum retains 30% on any sales. — Deadline: September 6, 2026. Fee: $40 for up to 3 works. Prize: $500 / $250 / $150 + $100 People's Choice.

item.title: Best in Show · Kirkland Arts Center
item.description: Kirkland Arts Center's first annual juried exhibition, built around the animals we live with. Each year the centre picks a different animal and leaves the interpretation entirely open; the 2026 subject is dogs, real or imaginary, abstract or representational. The call is open to Washington-based 2D and 3D artists of all ages working in any medium — photography included — with work no larger than 48 inches in height or width. Selected pieces are shown from 18 September to 9 October 2026 with an opening reception on 18 September, and a $500 prize goes to one winner in each of the 2D and 3D categories. Artists ship or deliver their own work ready to hang or display and include return postage; the centre takes 40% commission on sales. KAC was founded in 1962 and has occupied the historic Peter Kirk Building, built in 1893, for more than sixty years. — Deadline: July 31, 2026. Fee: $30. Prize: $500 2D + $500 3D.

item.title: Athenaeum Gallery Show Proposals · Northern Virginia Fine Arts Association
item.description: The Athenaeum Gallery, a Greek Revival landmark in Old Town Alexandria run by the Northern Virginia Fine Arts Association, sets aside part of its programme for shows proposed by artists and curators rather than chosen by the gallery director. Artists living or working in Virginia, Maryland or the District of Columbia may propose a solo show; groups of artists from the region may propose a group show; and a curator based anywhere may propose a show of work by artists from the area. Proposals are reviewed by gallery director Twig Murray on what the artist is trying to communicate, what makes the work distinctive, technical quality, and how recently the artist has shown locally. All visual media are welcome, photography included, but every work must be wall-mounted, less than nine inches deep and ready to hang on picture hooks; nothing floor-standing and nothing requiring electricity. The gallery takes 40% commission on sales. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: $40. Prize: Solo or group exhibition.

item.title: CCA Call for Exhibition Proposals 2026
item.description: Coconino Center for the Arts in Flagstaff, managed by Creative Flagstaff, invites exhibition proposals from artists, curators and cultural organisations for rolling review by its Exhibitions Selection Committee. The building holds a 4,000 square foot Main Gallery, which programmes three to four major exhibitions a year, an adjacent 215 square foot Project Gallery with four to six shows a year, and a 200-seat theatre; it sits on US 180 on the road to the Grand Canyon and serves the arts, science and cultural communities of northern Arizona. Interdisciplinary proposals involving digital media or installation are particularly encouraged. A proposal runs one to two pages covering theme, description, fit with the centre's mission and calendar availability, plus a bio, a two-page resume with recent and upcoming exhibitions, and up to ten work samples (images, audio or video). The application fee is $10 and Flagstaff Arts Council retains 30% commission on sales. — Deadline: December 31, 2026. Fee: $10. Prize: Gallery exhibition.

item.title: Rosewood Arts Center 2027 Exhibition Proposals
item.description: The Kettering Health Art Gallery at Rosewood Arts Center, run by the City of Kettering just outside Dayton, Ohio, presents six to eight solo exhibitions a year by emerging local, regional and national artists, and is taking proposals for its 2027 season running January to December. Artists working in any media may apply, including video and installation. A proposal consists of a cover letter describing the exhibition, any special installation requirements, possible public programmes and available dates; an artist statement, resume and exhibition record; and ten images with titles, media, dimensions and dates — the selection committee sees only those ten. Rosewood also welcomes proposals for accompanying educational programmes, community projects and artist talks. Three regional arts professionals make the recommendations and everyone is notified by 10 September 2026. Selected artists receive a $300 honorarium; the city insures all work while on exhibition and covers printing and mailing of an announcement for each show. Open to adults living in the United States, though current City of Kettering employees are not eligible for solo exhibitions. — Deadline: August 27, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: $300 honorarium + Solo exhibition.

item.title: Showcase 2027 · Northwind Art
item.description: Northwind Art's Showcase programme fills the Jeanette Best Gallery on Water Street in Port Townsend, Washington with roughly thirty-six artists a year, arranged in three cohorts that each hang for about four months: 28 January – 10 May, 13 May – 6 September, and 9 September 2027 – 3 January 2028. Jurors look for a cohesive body of work and pay particular attention to retail pricing, aiming to select artists whose work generally sits under $1,000. The programme is geared towards artists in Jefferson, Clallam, Mason, Kitsap and Island counties but the application is open to artists outside them; Showcase artists may not be represented by another gallery or retail outlet in Port Townsend during their run. Ten images are required, each with dimensions, medium and retail price, and no imagery derived from AI. The selection panel is made up of two Northwind Art exhibits staff, exhibit designer Suzanne Lamon and executive director Martha Worthley. The $35 fee is waived on the honour system for artists from historically underrepresented BIPOC and LGBTQIA+ communities. Everyone is notified by 5 December 2026. — Deadline: November 12, 2026. Fee: $35 (free for BIPOC and LGBTQIA+ artists). Prize: Gallery exhibition.

item.title: Art Edu 2026 · Art Center Waco
item.description: A juried exhibition at Art Center Waco celebrating art educators as practising artists — the work they make beyond the classroom, which so often feeds back into how they teach. Active and retired art educators living in McLennan, Bell, Falls, Coryell, Limestone, Hill and Bosque Counties in central Texas may submit up to three original works made in the last five years. All 2D and 3D media are eligible, photography included; reproductions of original works such as giclée prints are not, though photographic prints are. Work can be up to 72 inches in any direction and wall pieces up to 60 pounds, and artworks previously exhibited at ACW are not eligible. The show hangs in the Beard Gallery from 29 October to 19 December 2026. Entry is $25 and the centre takes 30% commission, with proceeds supporting its exhibitions, education programmes and community work. — Deadline: September 27, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: 24th National Fine Art Show · Peninsula Art League
item.description: The Peninsula Art League's annual juried show, now in its 24th year, returns to the Gig Harbor Vintage Aero Museum — a hangar of restored vintage aircraft that the League has turned into an exhibition venue. Photography and digital art are judged alongside two- and three-dimensional work, and the two jurors come from Pacific Northwest museums: Jessica Wilks, Director of Curatorial and Interpretation at Tacoma Art Museum, who has led curatorial teams for more than twenty years and shapes TAM's commitment to artists of the region; and Greg Robinson, Chief Curator at the Bainbridge Island Museum of Art, formerly director of the Museum of Northwest Art and a Betty Bowen Award committee member. More than $8,500 in cash prizes will be awarded. Open to artists 18 and over anywhere in the country; work must be original, made in the last two years, and not produced in a class or workshop. AI tools may be used in a supporting role for editing or minor enhancement but may not generate the artwork. Nudes, religious symbols, political themes and extreme violence will not be considered. All work must be for sale with a 15% commission; 2D pieces need D-rings and taut wire, no sawtooth hangers. Shipped work is accepted, at a $20 handling fee per piece. Jurying finishes 27 October and everyone is notified by 29 October. The show runs 14 November – 2 December 2026. — Deadline: October 18, 2026. Fee: $55 first entry ($45 members) + $10 each addl. Prize: $8,500 in cash awards + Group exhibition.

item.title: 2nd Annual Kit Gilbert Juried Showcase · Ross Lynn Charitable Foundation
item.description: An open, themeless juried showcase at the Gilbert Center in downtown Ruston, Louisiana — a legacy project of the Ross Lynn Charitable Foundation that carries forward the work of two local artists, Ross Lynn and Kit Gilbert, the Ruston painter this annual show is named for. There is no set subject: any original work made since 2020 is welcome, and photography is explicitly among the media considered alongside painting, sculpture, mixed media, textile, ceramics and short video. The juror is Julie Crews, an oil painter based in Huntsville, Alabama who keeps an open studio and gallery at the 122-year-old Lowe Mill Arts and Entertainment complex and paints the domestic scenes of her own life — backyard fires, children swimming, errands around town. Two cash awards: the Juror's Choice / Best-in-Show at $750, and a People's Choice at $500 voted by visitors on opening night. Open to US artists 18 and over, up to three works, each needing a 250-word artist statement. AI-generated work is not accepted. Photographs must be framed or mounted — unframed works on paper and unmounted prints will be rejected — and artists arrange their own delivery and return shipping. Notifications 19 October, work due 7 November, exhibition 16 November 2026 – 15 January 2027 with a reception on 19 November. The Gilbert Center takes 30% commission. — Deadline: October 5, 2026. Fee: $12 per artwork. Prize: $750 Best in Show + $500 People's Choice.

item.title: Artifacts · 6 Bridges Gallery
item.description: A juried exhibition at 6 Bridges Gallery, a fine art and craft gallery on Main Street in Maynard, Massachusetts, built around the marks, remnants and meaningful objects that shape how we understand the world. The gallery is looking for work that uncovers the traces of what remains — hidden histories, personal relics, the quiet evidence of lives lived — and asks artists to think about what we carry forward, whether physical, emotional, cultural or imagined. All media are welcome except video and AI-generated work. The juror is Claudia Fiks, an independent curator and arts administrator of more than twenty years who founded and directs TAG | The Art Gallery at the New England Art Center in Boston's SoWa Art & Design District, directs Newton Open Studios, and writes on contemporary art for Artscope Magazine; she says she values authenticity, risk-taking, and work that communicates beyond the surface, regardless of medium or career stage. Open to artists 16 and over, up to three works made in the last three years, wired and ready to hang (no sawtooth hangers) and no larger than 40 inches in any direction. Three awards are given: the Artifact Award, Jurors' Choice and People's Choice. All work must be for sale and artists keep 60%. Work must be hand-delivered — the gallery does not accept shipped artwork. Notifications 9 September, drop-off 30 September – 3 October, exhibition 7 October – 14 November 2026 with a reception on 17 October. — Deadline: August 16, 2026. Fee: $35 first entry + $5 each addl. Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: 26th Annual Juried Fine Art Show & Sale · Rockwall Art League
item.description: A three-day juried show and sale run by the Rockwall Art League in North Texas, open to artists across a five-state region — Texas, Oklahoma, Arkansas, Louisiana and New Mexico — and now in its 26th year. Photography is one of eight judged categories, alongside oil, watercolour, acrylic, mixed media, mosaic, drawing and sculpture, and up to $6,600 in cash prizes is awarded across them — $1,000 for Best in Show, $500 and $200 for first and second in each category, plus a run of ribbon-only special awards. The two judges are Dana Brock, an abstract and mixed-media painter and Signature Member of the Southwestern Watercolor Society, and Rachel Townsend Cerny, founder of RTown Gallery in historic downtown Grapevine, Texas. The League says it exists to give both established and emerging artists a platform, and the event puts work in front of collectors and business representatives from across the DFW metroplex. Open to artists 18 and over; work must be original and made after 1 January 2024, and compositions based on published material, other artists' work, or generated with AI are not eligible. Work made in a class or workshop is out, as is anything containing nudes, conspicuously religious content, drug references or blatant political statements. Up to two works per artist, submitted with two to five images. New for 2026: hand delivery only — shipped work is not accepted — 2D pieces capped at 36 x 36 inches including frame, sculpture under 50 lbs, and a new venue at The Center at Rockwall City Place. Notifications go out 26 September; take-in is the morning of 16 October and the show runs 16–18 October 2026, with awards announced at the 16 October reception and final awards on the 18th. — Deadline: September 15, 2026. Fee: $45 for up to 2 entries ($35 members) + $5 each addl. Prize: Up to $6,600 in cash prizes.

item.title: Summertime: Long Days, Lazy Days, Gentle Breezes · Arizona Photography Alliance
item.description: The second Juried Theme Gallery call of 2026 from the Arizona Photography Alliance, a Scottsdale-based non-profit now in its third year of online juried exhibitions. The brief is deliberately broad — summer as long days, lazy days and gentle breezes — and work in any medium is welcome, analogue, digital or alternative process, though AI-generated photography is not accepted. Independent juror Claire A. Warden, an interdisciplinary artist working in still and moving image whose cameraless abstraction has appeared in Harper's Magazine, Der Greif, Strange Fire Collective, Lenscratch and Light Work's Contact Sheet, selects one first-place winner for a $100 cash award plus two honourable mentions featured on AZPA's website and social channels. Every entrant is represented in the resulting virtual gallery — the juror picks one image from each submission — and all entrants may offer their chosen image for sale, handling any transaction directly. Open to members and non-members alike; joining brings the fee down to $25. AZPA board members may not enter. Submissions run August 1–16, 2026 through CaFÉ, with notifications on 30 August and the gallery going live on 1 September. — Deadline: August 16, 2026. Fee: $25 members, $50 non-members. Prize: $100 + Online exhibition.

item.title: Seen/Unseen at Eric Fischl Gallery · Arizona Photography Alliance
item.description: A portfolio-based call from the Arizona Photography Alliance for a gallery exhibition at the Eric Fischl Gallery, perched atop Phoenix College's Fine Arts Building with panoramic views of central Phoenix. Seen/Unseen invites the full range of photographic methods and styles — from the tangible world we perceive to the hidden meanings and emotional states we sense — and asks for a cohesive body of work rather than single images. The juror is Emilia Mickevicius, Norton Family Assistant Curator of Photography in a curatorial post shared between Phoenix Art Museum and the Center for Creative Photography, previously curatorial assistant in SFMOMA's photography department, where she worked on Sightlines, Kinship: Photography and Connection and Sea Change. Selected applicants exhibit three to five works chosen from their submitted portfolio; all selected work is also presented as an online exhibition. Applicants must be current AZPA members at any level, though you need not live in Arizona — membership can be taken out at the time of applying. Accepted work must arrive exhibition-ready, shipped by 28 September or hand-delivered 29 September; the gallery retains 30% on sales. Exhibition runs 5–22 October 2026 with an opening reception on 5 October. — Deadline: August 23, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: 2026 Fall Members Juried Exhibition · Wayne Art Center
item.description: Wayne Art Center's autumn members' show in the Davenport Gallery outside Philadelphia, juried both for entry and for awards. Eligible media run from painting and works on paper through ceramics, glass, fiber and jewellery to photography and 3D printing, so it is one of the few regional all-media shows where lens-based work sits alongside craft. Each member may submit exactly one original work made after 1 January 2024 and not previously shown at WAC — no second CaFÉ accounts, no exceptions. The juror is Peter Van Dyck, a Philadelphia painter who trained at the Florence Academy of Art and has taught at the Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine Arts, with solo shows at John Pence Gallery, Eleanor Ettinger Gallery and The Grenning Gallery. Open to Wayne Art Center 2026/2027 adult members aged 18 and over; membership can be taken out before applying. All accepted work must be hand-delivered to and collected from the centre — nothing shipped. Notifications 22 August, hand delivery 1 September, exhibition 8 September – 3 October 2026, with a reception and awards presentation on 20 September. — Deadline: August 5, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: Celebrating Color · Edgewater Gallery
item.description: A national juried group exhibition at Edgewater Gallery, an artist-owned collective that has been part of downtown Fort Bragg on California's Mendocino Coast since 2003. The show takes colour in any form or dimension as its subject — atmosphere, emotion, memory, and the way chroma changes what we see — and the gallery says it is especially interested in work with a distinctive relationship to colour, whether through intensity, harmony, contrast, material presence or unexpected combinations. Photography is explicitly among the accepted media, alongside painting, drawing, printmaking, mixed media, collage, fiber, sculpture and ceramics; AI-generated work, video and installation are not accepted. Open to artists 18 and over living in the United States, up to three works each, all of which must be original, for sale, and available for the full run. Two-dimensional work must be ready to hang without sawtooth hangers, and pieces must fit through a standard door. The four jurors are all working artists: ceramicist Alexis Moyer, mixed-media abstractionist Chris Hagie, painter Gwen Lowery, and Karin Denson, whose glitch-based paintings, photomontages and collages sit between nature and technology. Jury results 7 September, work due by 25 September, exhibition 1 October – 2 November 2026 with an opening reception on 2 October. The gallery takes 40% commission. — Deadline: August 28, 2026. Fee: $35 + $5 each additional work. Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: Circuito OFF 2026 · NARNIMMAGINARIA
item.description: The free and independent section of NARNIMMAGINARIA, the photography festival staged in the historic centre of Narni, Umbria, and run by the Associazione culturale SATOR. Now in its 11th edition, the 2026 theme is "Through human landscapes": the traces people leave in the places they inhabit and reshape, and the invisible territories of their stories and emotions. Documentary, narrative, conceptual, artistic and experimental readings are all admitted, and entry is open to photographers of any age, nationality or background. Three categories: Single Shot, a single photograph, with fine-art printing and installation handled entirely by the organisers; Triptych, three photographs or a single panel supplied already printed and hung in the bars, restaurants, shops and other businesses of the centre rather than in galleries, with installation optionally delegated to the organisers for €35; and Stories, a printed sequence of 8 to 18 images at 30×40 cm, framed by the organisers. Entrants can apply to one, two or all three categories and submit more than one work in each, paying a €15 contribution per category. Everything goes by email as a single ZIP folder. The exhibition runs 17 October to 2 November 2026; printed works are due 8 October. — Deadline: September 14, 2026. Fee: €15 per category. Prize: Festival exhibition.

item.title: ROOTS · Fototeka
item.description: Second open call from Fototeka, a Romanian analog photography hub and publisher, for a new collective printed volume following its first book Sequence 01, which brought together 93 photographers. The theme is ROOTS — origin, belonging, memory and connection, read literally or metaphorically: natural elements, portraits, archives, rituals, personal and collective histories. Roots usually remain hidden, yet they shape what becomes visible. Only film-based photography is eligible; digital and AI-generated images are excluded. Up to ten analog photographs per submission, minimum 3000 pixels on the long side. The 50 RON (about €10) fee supports the editorial, design, printing and presentation work and does not guarantee inclusion: the curatorial team sequences the book, so a submission may end up represented by no photographs, one, or several. Selected work may also be featured on Fototeka's online platforms. The album is planned for October–November 2026. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: 50 RON (~€10). Prize: Publication (print).

item.title: Under Many Moons: Asian and Pacific Islander Art, Identity, and Community · Sebastopol Center for the Arts
item.description: Juried exhibition at Sebastopol Center for the Arts presented with AAPIC North Bay and the Many Moons Festival, the annual autumn gathering in Sebastopol that uplifts Asian American and Pacific Islander culture, creativity and community. The show explores identity, heritage, belonging and cultural expression. While it centres AAPI voices and perspectives, artists of all backgrounds engaging thoughtfully with the themes are invited to submit work reflecting personal and collective narratives shaped by culture, place and lived experience. All media, photography included. Entry is $35 for one application of up to three images, with $10 for each additional application. Work must fit through a 7' by 7' gallery door and on an 8-foot wall; the centre's installation team can hang selected pieces. Juror Patricia Wakida is a community historian, linoleum block carver and letterpress printer who apprenticed as a papermaker in Gifu, Japan. Work must have been made in the last five years and not shown at SebArts before. Notifications 14 August; exhibition runs 26 September – 11 October 2026 with an opening reception on 26 September. — Deadline: August 4, 2026. Fee: $35 (3 images), $10 each additional. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: CCAN 2026 — 10th Annual National Juried Art Competition · Center for Contemporary Arts
item.description: Tenth edition of the Center for Contemporary Arts' national juried competition in downtown Abilene, Texas. Over $7,000 is awarded annually across 11 media categories — including a dedicated 2D Photography (Film & Digital) category, each with a $500 first prize — plus a $750 juror's award and a $1,000 best of show. Juror Carlyn Ray is a Dallas-based glass artist known for large-scale installations. Open to artists 18 and over; work must be original, made within the last three years, and the image submitted must be the piece delivered. Wall-mounted 2D work is capped at 48 inches framed on its longest dimension, wall-mounted 3D at 36 by 36 inches and freestanding 3D at 36 inches in any dimension, with a 50 lb weight limit. No video or mural work. Entry is $35 for one image and $20 for each additional, limit three. Notifications 1 September; exhibition runs 10 October – 21 November 2026, with the opening reception and awards on 10 October. — Deadline: August 22, 2026. Fee: $35 for 1 image, $20 each additional. Prize: $7,000 in cash awards.

item.title: Contemporary Figures: A National Juried Exhibition · LHUCA
item.description: National juried exhibition of contemporary figurative work at LHUCA, the Louise Hopkins Underwood Center for the Arts in Lubbock, Texas. The call asks how the body is understood in relation to environment, society and technology: scientific advances have made us more aware of the composition and processes of the human body while blurring the boundaries between the human and the nonhuman, and the body remains intimately tied to identity and to how we move in space and in relation to others. Figurative work addressing a range of themes and presenting the body in unique ways is welcome. Open to painting, drawing, printmaking, mixed media, collage, photography, digital art, ceramics, books and textiles; all works must hang on the wall and are capped at 36 by 36 inches, with plexiglass glazing required on anything shipped. Open to artists 18 or over living in the United States. Entry is $25 for up to two images. Cash prizes of $300, $200 and $100 plus a $50 honorable mention. Notifications 11 September 2026; the exhibition runs 2 October – 28 November 2026, with opening receptions on 2 October and 6 November during the First Friday Art Trail, which draws an estimated 5,000 visitors a month to LHUCA's galleries. — Deadline: September 6, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: $300 / $200 / $100.

item.title: Call for Proposals 2027 · LHUCA
item.description: LHUCA invites exhibition proposals for its 2027–2028 gallery season in Lubbock, Texas. Four galleries are available and each exhibition runs two consecutive months. All visual art media are accepted, including photography. Free to apply: submit a PDF with 5–10 digital images, an artist statement of up to 500 words, contact details and preferred dates. An artist stipend is available for travelling artists, and work can be for sale or not. Proposals are encouraged but not required to respond to the character of a particular gallery; floor plans are published alongside the call. Artists who have exhibited with LHUCA before can only reapply every five years. The galleries draw an estimated 5,000-plus visitors a month during the First Friday Art Trail. — Deadline: September 13, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Chaos: An Exploration of Disorder, Meaning, and Possibility · Bitfactory Gallery
item.description: Juried exhibition at Bitfactory Gallery & Studios in Denver seeking two-dimensional, wall-hanging work that responds to chaos — visible or invisible, personal or collective, destructive or generative. It may appear as a fractured system, an unsettled world, a difficult relationship, a crowded mind, or the moment when certainty gives way; it may be imposed on us, created by us, or necessary before change can occur. Literal, emotional, psychological, social, symbolic and abstract approaches are all welcome. All 2D mediums qualify, including photography, painting, collage, fiber and textile, pastel, graphite and print works. Open to Colorado residents aged 18 and over; 3–10 images, $25 entry with $5 per additional image. Juror W. Max Thomason. Notifications 10 August; exhibition runs 21 August – 12 September 2026 with an opening reception on 21 August, 6–9pm. — Deadline: August 9, 2026. Fee: $25 for 3 images, $5 each additional. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 2026 Juried Exhibition · Rawls Museum Arts
item.description: Annual all-media juried exhibition at Rawls Museum Arts, a non-profit museum founded in 1958 in Courtland, Virginia, dedicated to making the arts accessible through exhibitions, education and community outreach. $1,000 in total prize money: $500 first place, $300 second and $200 third. Artists of all ages are encouraged to apply. Work must be original and created without the aid of an instructor or kit; AI-generated work, or work derived in whole or part from AI, is not eligible. Entry is $35 for up to three submissions, one image per artwork. Pieces cannot exceed 50 pounds or 45 inches in the longest dimension, and all selected work must be hand-delivered — no shipping — by 2pm on 12 September 2026. Co-curated by museum staff with juror Allen TenBusschen, a contemporary realist painter who chairs the art department at the University of Lynchburg. Notifications by 15 August; exhibition runs 19 September – 23 October 2026, and the museum takes a 30% commission on sales. — Deadline: July 31, 2026. Fee: $35 for 3 works. Prize: $500 / $300 / $200.

item.title: Common Ground in the Heartland: Reflecting on America at 250 · Washington Pavilion Visual Arts Center
item.description: Free-to-enter juried exhibition at the Visual Arts Center of the Washington Pavilion in Sioux Falls, marking the 250th anniversary of the United States. The centre invites artists from across the Midwest to reflect on the people, places and experiences that shape a shared story — from small towns and family farms to growing cities and tribal communities — in a region long a crossroads of cultures, traditions, industries and ideas. The exhibition explores the values, traditions and relationships that bring people together while recognising the diverse experiences that define communities, with suggested themes including community and belonging, cultural heritage, land and stewardship. All mediums are welcome, photography included, and up to five images may be submitted. Artists from the Midwest or with a connection to the region are encouraged to apply, though entry is not formally restricted, and artists at every career stage are invited. Work must not exceed 60 inches or 50 lbs and arrives ready to install; the centre insures it and splits sales 70/30 in the artist's favour. Notifications 5 August, with work due 20 August — the show then runs an unusually long 28 August 2026 – 21 February 2027. — Deadline: July 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: REBUILDING: Art as Renewal, Possibility, and Purpose · Art League Rhode Island
item.description: Juried exhibition at the Art League Rhode Island Gallery and Tiernan Hallway Gallery in Pawtucket, asking how art can restore what has been fractured — making whole what has been broken, empowering what has been silenced and reclaiming what connects us. The theme is not about loss but about what gets built next: how art can reassemble meaning, mend relationships and model balance in a world seeking repair. Open to any artist 18 or over, in all 2D and 3D media; 1–5 images plus an optional video, $35 entry with $10 per additional media file. Work must be original and previously unexhibited with ALRI, and anything conceived or created with generative AI is ineligible. Jurors are Kerry Phillips, a Miami-based installation artist working with found objects and site-responsive materials, and Meaghan Kent, independent curator, founder of the nonprofit Site95 and former Deputy Director at MOCA North Miami. Awards are $500 first, $300 second and $150 third, plus two honorable mentions and a People's Choice. Notification by 4 November; exhibition runs 5 December 2026 – 17 January 2027. — Deadline: October 11, 2026. Fee: $35 (1–5 images), $10 each additional. Prize: $500 / $300 / $150.

item.title: Fresh Squeezed 2026 Annual Juried Show · Suffolk Art League
item.description: The Suffolk Art League's annual juried exhibition at the Suffolk Art Gallery in Suffolk, Virginia, marking the league's 50th anniversary and asking for artists' latest, never-before-seen work. Open to artists over 18 in all mediums: the gallery's own listing rules out only video and audio, though the CaFÉ entry also excludes digital, so anyone printing digitally is worth checking with first. Work must not have been previously exhibited at the gallery and must have been completed within the last two years. Members submit up to three works for $30; non-members pay $55 and full-time student non-members $50, both of which include an individual membership. First place is $500 plus the opportunity to present a one-person show at the Suffolk Art Gallery in 2027, with $300 second and $200 third. 2D work must be framed, wired or gallery-wrapped — no sawtooth hangers — and 3D work is displayed on pedestals provided by the gallery. Notifications by 25 September; exhibition runs 24 October – 4 December 2026. The league retains a 30% consignment on works sold. — Deadline: September 16, 2026. Fee: $55 non-members ($30 members), +$5 each extra. Prize: $500 + Solo exhibition.

item.title: Backwards/Forwards · Light Art Space
item.description: Juried exhibition of handmade prints at Light Art Space in Silver City, New Mexico, staged as the juried show of the Southwest Print Fiesta. The brief asks artists to treat time as material — memory, pressure, inheritance, repetition, rupture and possibility — looking backward at the histories that shape us and forward at futures we imagine or fear. All work must be handmade prints made by the artist in the last five years using traditional printmaking and/or photographic processes: silver gelatin, photopolymer and copperplate gravure, cyanotype, vandyke, gum bichromate, palladium, platinum, carbon, salt, chemigram, lumen, argyrotype, oil print, chlorophyll, instant transfers and lifts, alongside etching, woodcut, lithography, screenprint and letterpress. 3D and experimental work encouraged. Digital processes are allowed only where meaningfully integrated with handmade methods; AI-generated and purely digital prints are ineligible. Juror Terran J. Last Gun, Piikani artist based in Santa Fe and an Art in America 2026 New Talent. Open worldwide to artists 18 and over. $35 for three works, $10 per additional piece up to ten, $20 for full-time students. Work must arrive ready to hang but framing is not required. Exhibition runs 8 October – 7 November 2026 with a reception and juror talk on 9 October; gallery takes 50% on sales and artists cover shipping both ways. — Deadline: September 13, 2026. Fee: $35 for 3 works. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: PhEST Portfolio Reviews 2026
item.description: Free portfolio reviews at PhEST – See Beyond the Sea, the international photography and contemporary art festival in Monopoli, Puglia. Reviews run 8 August (3–6pm) and 9 August (10am–1pm) at the Saint Leonardo Monastery, in 20-minute one-to-one sessions; each photographer can book up to three reviews, one per reviewer. Completed projects and work in progress are both welcome, presented as prints or on a device. The 2026 reviewers are Josh Lustig, picture editor at FT Weekend Magazine; Erik Vroons, writer and editor at Over Magazine; Veronica Daltri, photo editor at Il Manifesto; Krzysztof Candrowicz, curator and co-founder of Łódź Fotofestiwal; artist and curator Francesca Seravalle; and Hannah Watson, director of Trolley Books. Sessions with Lustig, Vroons, Candrowicz and Watson are held in English only. Registration is free and online until 2 August, with limited on-site places from 10 minutes before each session. — Deadline: August 2, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: None listed.
